findings.motion: HB 958, Election Law Changes, Second Reading (Senate vote 693)
findings.note: Senate second-reading vote on HB 958 (passed 28 to 13). His vote is listed as No. The ratified bill (https://www.ncleg.gov/Sessions/2025/Bills/House/PDF/H958v9.pdf) makes registration forms at driver license offices and county boards proceed only if the applicant affirmatively states US citizenship (new G.S. 163-83, with a 30-day sworn-statement notice for blank answers), and requires a process to remove voters flagged as non-citizens from a federal database. It has no photo ID or ID-number rule. He also voted No on amendments 1, 5 and on motions to table amendments 2, 3, 6, 7, 8, 9, 10 the same evening (votes 684-692).

Listed as a cosponsor (not primary) of SB 457, Automatic Voter Registration. The bill registers eligible people automatically through driver license offices, public agencies and colleges, keeps the question asking whether the applicant is a US citizen, and bars ineligible people from applying. Referred to committee and not enacted. It sets no ID rule for voting.

findings.motion: Senate second reading, H 958 Election Law Changes (28-13)
findings.note: Listed among the Noes on the Senate second-reading vote on H 958, the election law changes bill. The ratified bill (https://www.ncleg.gov/Sessions/2025/Bills/House/PDF/H958v9.pdf) requires a registration application to state that the applicant is a U.S. citizen before it is processed, with a 30-day sworn-statement fix if the answer is blank, and sets up a process to remove voters flagged as possible non-citizens by a federal database. The bill page shows a Governor's veto on 2026-08-17.
subjects: federal database checks of voter rolls for non-citizens
